accepted_step.derivation: Re-derive from step 1: a path is a length-18 string s over {R,D} with nine R and nine D; position k records the k-th move. Let R(k) and D(k) be prefix counts in s_1..s_k. The path is at (R(k),D(k)) after k moves, since R increases x by 1 and D increases y by 1. Thus the path visits cell (a,b) exactly when some k satisfies R(k)=a and D(k)=b. Because R(k)+D(k)=k, this can only happen at k=a+b, so visiting (a,b) is equivalent to the prefix of length a+b having exactly a R moves. Since the prefix length is a+b, having a R moves also means having (a+b)-a=b D moves. Conversely, if the prefix of length a+b has a R moves and b D moves, then after those a+b moves the path is at (a,b). Therefore forbidding a visit to (a,b) is exactly forbidding strings whose prefix of length a+b contains a R moves, equivalently whose count-prefix (a,b) occurs. Applying this to the five forbidden cells gives: (2,2) forbids prefix length 4 with 2 R; (4,3) forbids prefix length 7 with 4 R; (5,6) forbids prefix length 11 with 5 R; (7,5) forbids prefix length 12 with 7 R; (8,8) forbids prefix length 16 with 8 R. A valid string must avoid all five prefix-count conditions. These exclusions are independent of the no-RRR/no-DDD condition and of the checkpoint condition.
accepted_step.goal: Translate each forbidden cell (a,b) into a prefix condition: after k moves #R=a and #D=b; exclude strings whose prefixes reach those counts.
accepted_step.result: For each forbidden cell (a,b), exclude strings where the prefix of length a+b has exactly a R moves (hence b D moves), i.e. the count-prefix (a,b) occurs. Concretely exclude: prefix length 4 with 2 R; length 7 with 4 R; length 11 with 5 R; length 12 with 7 R; length 16 with 8 R.

use.method: Public prefix-count check. A monotone path's k-th move is position k in the length-18 string; after k moves the coordinates are (#R in first k positions, #D in first k positions). For a cell (a,b), since #R+#D=k, a visit can occur only at k=a+b, and then #R=a, #D=b. Applying this to each forbidden cell reproduces the returned exclusion list: (2,2) -> k=4 with 2 R; (4,3) -> k=7 with 4 R; (5,6) -> k=11 with 5 R; (7,5) -> k=12 with 7 R; (8,8) -> k=16 with 8 R. I also checked the converse on a concrete prefix: the length-4 prefix RDRD has 2 R and 2 D, giving (2,2), so it is correctly excluded. Thus the returned step is the exact prefix condition for avoiding those cells.
use.result: agrees: each forbidden cell (a,b) is excluded exactly by the condition that the prefix of length a+b contains a R moves (and hence b D moves); the listed pairs are (4,2R), (7,4R), (11,5R), (12,7R), (16,8R).
